source: NCERT Class VII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Geography Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. A Land of Great Diversity
points: India has an **enormous variety of landforms** — mountains, plains, plateaus, deserts, coasts and islands.
This diversity shapes **climate, rivers, vegetation, farming and ways of life**.
India is broadly divided into **major physiographic (relief) divisions**.

sections.heading: 2. The Himalayan Mountains
points: **Young fold mountains** in the north; the world's **highest** ranges.
Three parallel ranges: **Himadri (Greater Himalayas — highest, permanent snow)**, **Himachal (Middle)**, **Shivalik (Outer, lowest)**.
Source of great **rivers (Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra)**; act as a **climatic barrier** and a natural defence.

sections.heading: 3. The Northern Plains
points: Formed by the **alluvium (silt)** deposited by the **Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra** river systems.
**Flat, fertile and densely populated** — the agricultural heartland ('the granary').
Old alluvium = **bhangar**; new alluvium = **khadar** (more fertile).

sections.heading: 4. Plateau, Desert, Coasts and Islands
points: **Peninsular Plateau** — old, stable, **mineral-rich**; includes the **Deccan Plateau**, bordered by the **Western and Eastern Ghats**.
**Thar (Great Indian) Desert** — hot, sandy, in the north-west (Rajasthan).
**Coastal Plains** — along the Arabian Sea (**western**) and Bay of Bengal (**eastern**); ports, fishing, farming.
**Islands** — the **Andaman & Nicobar** (Bay of Bengal) and **Lakshadweep** (Arabian Sea, coral).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Physiographic divisions: Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Thar Desert, Coastal Plains, Islands.
Himalayan ranges: Himadri (highest) > Himachal > Shivalik (lowest).
Northern Plains = alluvium of Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra; bhangar (old) vs khadar (new).
Peninsular/Deccan Plateau = old, mineral-rich; bordered by Western & Eastern Ghats.
Islands: Andaman & Nicobar (Bay of Bengal), Lakshadweep (Arabian Sea, coral).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Himalayan ranges (N→S): **Himadri (Greater) → Himachal (Middle) → Shivalik (Outer)** — Himadri is highest.
**Khadar** (new alluvium) is **more fertile** than **bhangar** (old).
**Lakshadweep** is in the **Arabian Sea** (coral); **Andaman & Nicobar** in the **Bay of Bengal**.
The **Peninsular Plateau** is **old and stable**, unlike the **young** Himalayas.
